items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law and the economic development law, in relation to the creation of the empire state digital gaming media production credit; and providing for the repeal of certain provisions upon expiration thereof
items.lawCode: Add §44, amd §§210-B & 606, Tax L; amd §352, add §242, Ec Dev L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5887

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the tax law and the economic
development law, in relation to the creation of the empire state
digital gaming media production credit; and providing for the repeal
of certain provisions upon expiration thereof

 PURPOSE :

To remake the digital media gaming adopted in Part K of the SF 2016
Revenue bill into a "below-the-line" production credit This will allow
both the industries to accurately calculate the benefits of the
programs, allow the State to better monitor the credits, and to ease
access to the incentives. Both industries are of the opinion that the
credits as currently in statute are unworkable and are actually
serving as a deterrent to growth for New York companies.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one creates a new section forty-four in the Tax Law to provide
a production incentive for the creation of video gaming in New York.

Subdivision (a) lays out eligibility criteria for companies that file
under the corporate franchise or personal income taxes.

Subdivision (b) limits the annual amount of refundable credits
available under the program to no more than $50 million a year,
allocates the available credits to three regions of the state, namely
New York City at fifty percent of the total credit allocations per
year, the metro New York suburbs at twenty percent and Upstate at
thirty percent. A project must perform at least 60 percent of eligible
costs within a region to qualify for credits in that region.

Subdivision (c) defines eligible "below the line" costs and qualified
productions.

Sections 2, 3 and 4 establish the credit in Articles 9-A and 22 of the
Tax Law.

Section 5 authorizes the Commissioner of Economic Development to
establish corresponding regulations and procedures to allow for the
effective administration of the credit.

Section 6 eliminates digital gaming as qualifying for the Excelsior
job creation credit to remove the possibility of double dipping at
taxpayer expense.

Section 7 creates a new section 243 in the economic development law
for reporting requirements for the new program. Reports will be filed
by ESDC on a biannual basis to be sent to the Director of the Budget
and the fiscal chairs of the legislature. The reports must detail the
amount of credits claimed and paid, the number of projects by size and
region, and the name of the taxpayer or taxpaying entity receiving the
credits.

In addition, every third year ESDC will be required to produce and
present a report to the Executive and the Legislature prepared by an
independent third party on how the programs are operating and the
overall economic impact of the program on the State economy.

Section 8 contains the effective date of the act and a five year
sunset to the programs.

 JUSTIFICATION :


This bill is designed to provide meaningful and effective incentives
to an industry essential to the future of the State. Provisions hoping
to aid and incent digital gaming production in New York State were
included in the adopted SFY 16 Budget, but unfortunately, it now
appears that those incentives fail to provide any real boosts to these
industries. The bill would transfer incentives from the existing the
Excelsior program, and support production activities occurring for
digital gaming in the State similar to the type of support New York
provides to the film industry. The need for a functioning incentive
program can be seen in that New York currently only generates a tiny
fraction of video and other digital gaming, with only one percent of
the U.S. $25 billion industry, and an insignificant blip of the $70
billion worldwide gaming industry generated in New York.

What is truly disconcerting about these numbers is that New York is
undoubtedly the home of the most creative individuals in the industry,
and graduates the finest game developers anywhere. We need robust and
accessible programs to encourage these creative geniuses to work and
perform in the State, and aid an industry that has a potential for
exponential growth both in Down and Up State.

Aiding the video and other digital gaming industry through the
Excelsior program has been an utter failure as no one is aware of any
claims for credits for the industry since the industry was made
eligible in over two years ago. Consequently, the industry has
approached the Legislature for a different, more strategic and easier
to access program.

This bill has received universal support from everyone involved in the
gaming industries. The bill provides for true "below the line"
production credits that will exponentially grow the industries in New
York, and create employment while not providing taxpayer funds for
"owners and directors". In order to not to place any strains on the
State budget, the credit is capped at $50 million a year.

The bill also provides for strong reporting requirements to determine
if the incentives will produce significant company revenue and
permanent employment growth in the State.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S.7485-B - veto memo 255.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Up to $50 million a year in tax expenditures.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately and shall apply to taxable years beginning on or after
January 1, 2018, and will be deemed to expire and be repealed on
December 31, 2022.

summary: Establishes the empire state digital gaming media production credit; provides such credit shall be calculated as a percentage of eligible production costs incurred within this state; provides such credits be allocated on a regional basis; limits credits to an aggregate of twenty-five million dollars per year.
